title: The Nameless King
snippet:
The Nameless King -  Dark Souls III - boss - description 
 description : The Nameless King was once a dragon-slaying god of war, before he sacrificed everything to ally himself with the ancient dragons.

title: Lord Gwyn's Firstborn
snippet:
Long ago, the Nameless King was a god of war and heir to lightning. The firstborn was a god of war, and inherited sunlight, which manifests as lightning.
The Nameless King wielded the Dragonslayer Swordspear, a weapon from the Age of Gods. The firstborn similarly wielded a great spear.
The firstborn eventually committed a grave error in the eyes of Anor Londo, which led to the rescinding of his deific status and his removal from the annals of history, his name forgotten. The Nameless King sacrificed everything to ally with the ancient dragons, whom he once fought.
The Nameless King wore a crown and bracelets that greatly resemble those once worn by Gwyn, the First Lord.
Dragon Slayer Ornstein, once the faithful first knight of the Sun's firstborn, left Anor Londo in the dragonless age in search of the Nameless King. His weapon, a cross spear, is extremely similar to that wielded by the Nameless King.

title: The Nameless King
snippet:
The Nameless King -  Dark Souls III - boss - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : The Nameless King is the firstborn child of Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight and one of the deities who resided in Anor Londo during the Age of Fire. He was worshipped by humans as the "god of war".

title: The Nameless King
snippet:
The Nameless King -  Dark Souls III - boss - phase_2_the_nameless_king 
 phase_2_the_nameless_king : The Nameless King will dismount and absorb the strength of his mount after it is defeated. His attacks will be dragged out when going after the player. Usually catching an unprepared fighter off guard as they roll too early and are struck for heavy damage. Which on later a play through, can nearly one hit the player in several instances. His attacks will either be followed with large burst of wind, or lightning and he also possesses several attacks that can release ranged bolts on the player. Along with a grab that can travel up to 20 units in the player's direction.

It is advised that the player wait for him to finish his attacks before attacking him during his recovery from the combo, or strike him when he is stuck telegraphing his more powerful maneuvers.

title: Soul of the Nameless King

One of the twisted souls, steeped in strength.

Use to acquire many souls, or transpose to extract its true strength.

The Nameless King was once a dragon-slaying god of war, before he sacrificed everything to ally himself with the ancient dragons.

title: The Nameless King
snippet:
The Nameless King -  Dark Souls III - boss - notes 
 notes : Neither the Nameless King nor the King of the Storm can be parried, but can be poise-broken with successive attacks, which allows one to perform a riposte.
Despite his appearance, the Nameless King does not count as Hollow for the Hollowslayer Greatsword damage bonus.

title: The Nameless King
snippet: After his father Gwyn left to link the First Flame, the throne of Anor Londo would pass to the eldest son of the King; and so the Nameless King inherited the Sunlight of his father. He would thus wear the golden crown, and succeed his father's titles of "king of the gods" and "god of the sun". The Nameless King was said to be inferior to none in terms of military strength. Gwyn's firstborn preserved his father's design and instructions, shepherding humans on the path to the Linking of the First Flame to continue the Age of Fire. In fact, underneath Anor Londo, a city was built exclusively for the undead, with an altar inside for the firstborn of Gwyn, and the aim of guiding a chosen undead who would one day sacrifice themselves to the Flame. Inside the city was the Undead Parish, a church at the center of the cult of the burg and connected to the first test to start on the path of Firelinking and ring the first Bell of Awakening. Furthermore, the town was connected to the Firelink

title: The Nameless King
snippet:
The Nameless King -  Dark Souls III - boss - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : Over the centuries, the Nameless King would continue to lead a warrior's life and take part in countless battles, fighting alongside his stormdrake with whom he forged a relationship of profound camaraderie, coming to consider him as a comrade in arms as was an ancient custom among soldiers of the gods.

title: Soul of the Nameless King
snippet:
Soul of the Nameless King -  Dark Souls III - item - availability 
 availability : Obtained by defeating the Nameless King in Archdragon Peak.

title: The Nameless King
snippet:
The Nameless King -  Dark Souls III - boss - dark_souls_ii 
 dark_souls_ii : At some point the followers of the god of the sun reached Drangleic. In the Harvest Valley, a region under the control of Alken, the remains of an altar that venerated the Nameless King can be found in the form of an exact replica of his ancient statues, implying that the god of the sun was worshipped until the fall of the kingdom.

title: The Nameless King
snippet:
The Nameless King -  Dark Souls III - boss - theories 
 theories : It is possible to theorize that the name of Gwyn's firstborn was "Gwyn-**Sen**" (セン).
**Before linking the First Flame, Lord Gwyn had entrusted his "male children" with the task of shepherding humans into following his example, through the prophecy of the Chosen Undead. The Undead Burg was likely built under the reign of the firstborn, as a statue of him can be found near the Undead Parish. Consequently, it is possible to theorize that Sen's Fortress, created as a proving ground to access Anor Londo and obtain the Lordvessel, all steps required as proofs of the prophecy, was also created by the firstborn, thereby making its name "Sen's Fortress"(センの古城). The particle "Gwyn" before the name comes from the fact that Gwyn's other children, known and openly recognized as legitimate, carry it in their name like "Gwyn-evere" and "Gwyn-dolin".

title: The Nameless King
snippet: It is possible to theorize that Faraam is the name that the people of Forossa used in veneration of Gwyn's firstborn after his name was lost over the centuries. Not only does Faraam share with the Nameless King the title of "god of war", but the god was also able to bless the armor of Forossa Knights, whose helmet depicted a knight fighting an enormous dragon, implying that Faraam was not a "false" deity created by the legends of men but an active entity in the kingdom who was capable of performing the miracles of the ancient gods. The Lion Knights of Forossa, besides bearing the title "Lion" same as Gwyn's firstborn and first knight, were not only mighty but rabid warriors obsessed with fighting; Forossan knights knew only war and no other ways of living, to the point that they didn't even know what they were fighting for, similarly to the Nameless King who "had respect only for arms, and nothing else".

title: The Nameless King
snippet: The eldest son of Gwyn eventually decided to "sacrifice everything" to ally himself with the dragons. In the eyes of the other deities of Anor Londo, archenemies of the dragons, his actions amounted to an unforgivable sin; he was therefore dethroned and exiled from the city. The former king was deprived of his deific status, his statues destroyed and his name erased from the annals of history. Before leaving Anor Londo, the eldest left his sunlight blade miracle and ring on Gwyn's empty tomb in his mausoleum as a final farewell, still paying respects for his father. Now excommunicated from the pantheon of the gods and without a home, the god of war continued to watch closely over his warriors of the sunlight, listening to their prayers and rewarding the proofs of their exploits with his miracles of Sunlight Spear and Great Lightning Spear.

title: Nameless Blacksmith Deity
snippet:
Nameless Blacksmith Deity -  Dark Souls - character - about_their_fate 
 about_their_fate : They are one of the only two gods who are described as "nameless" across the whole series, the other one being the Nameless King from *Dark Souls III*, who is all but confirmed to be Lord Gwyn's Firstborn, whose name was erased from the annals of history for betraying the other gods and siding with the Ancient Dragons. In that case, it might be possible that the Nameless Blacksmith Deity incurred the wrath of the other gods of Anor Londo in a similar fashion, and was thus punished for it by having their name scrubbed from history as well.

title: Bonfire (Dark Souls III)
snippet:

:Backtrack a little from the Great Belfry bonfire and pull the lever, thus ringing the bell and summoning the Nameless King into the boss arena. The bonfire will appear once he has been defeated.

title: The Nameless King

title: The Nameless King
snippet: The Falconers, a group of mercenaries hired to protect the elites of Volgen, were still part of the covenant of those that worshipped the God of the Sun and possessed their Sunlight Medals. Moreover, in Lindelt, a "sacred land" known for its clerics and miracles, the Nameless King's miracles of Lightning Spear and Great Lightning Spear were preserved and passed down within its religion, although the names of the clan of gods and the sun god had been lost. Furthermore, some other miracles of the god such as the Sunlight Blade and the Sacred Oath appear to have been part of the lost culture of Olaphis, indicating a continuing tradition of the cult of the Nameless King, even if fragmentary, throughout the history of Drangleic.

title: The Nameless King
snippet:
The Nameless King -  Dark Souls III - boss - lead 
 lead : , alongside his Stormdrake known as the **King of the Storm**, is an optional boss in *Dark Souls III*. In the first phase of their fight, the player deals damage to the dragon mount, before fighting the King one-on-one in the second phase.

title: The Nameless King
snippet:
The Nameless King -  Dark Souls III - boss - phase_1_king_of_the_storm 
 phase_1_king_of_the_storm : The fight begins with the Nameless King entering on his mount from the midway point of the arena. He then proceeds to attack the player through either swipes and slams from his spear. Lightning bolts during flight and flames fired from his mount. Both have two qualifiers; one being that he touches down nearby the player and sprays a swatch of fire in their direction, to cover a large area. The other being when the player stays under the mounts body and is reminiscent of the Ancient Dragons attack of flying straight up and flooding the area under him with a long burst of fire. This can easily kill the player as it will stun them in the first hit, knocking them down and, hit them once again as they recover.

title: Licia of Lindeldt
snippet:
==Trivia==
In *Scholar of the First Sin'', if she is killed before being invaded by the Nameless Usurper, then said invader will not appear in Drangleic Castle or Undead Crypt, pointing to Lindeldt being the usurper. This could have been intended from the start of the design process, or was added in later as many players theorized the Nameless Usurper to be Licia since it donned her clothing, though only used a dagger.
Licia's in-game name refers to her as being from "Lindeldt", yet the rest of items which provide some lore about this place refer to it as "Lindelt", and even some have been corrected to this term in later revisions of the game.

title: Crown of the Old Iron King (helm)
snippet:
Crown of the Old Iron King (helm) -  Dark Souls II - armor - description 
 description : Crown of the Old Iron King who once ruled this land.

The King sunk below the scorching iron, met the one whose name must never be repeated, and became Ichorous Earth.

But these were events of long ago, and today, no one even remembers the King's name.

title: Soul of the Nameless King
snippet:
Soul of the Nameless King -  Dark Souls III - item - usage 
 usage : Consume to acquire 16,000 souls or transpose with Ludleth to create either the Storm Curved Sword, the Dragonslayer Swordspear or the Lightning Storm miracle.

title: Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight
snippet: After her father Gwyn linked the First Flame, his throne passed to his firstborn son who, in a betrayal of his father's legacy, chose to ally with the dragons, the ancient enemies of the gods, and was therefore dethroned, exiled and his name eradicated from history. She abandoned Anor Londo along with most other deities and moved to an unknown location. Sometime after her departure she married Flame God Flann.

title: The Nameless King
snippet: of wyverns. From the sun god they also soon learned how to infuse their weapons with the power of lightning, lethal against dragons, and the ancient techniques for hunting archdragons. Finally they learned to use his miracles which allowed them to manipulate the power of lightning. The cult of the Nameless King remained prevalent among the soldiery of Lothric until the last days of the kingdom, as one of his altars can be found right inside the military barracks, and the knights of the kingdom seem to still be part of the Warriors of Sunlight covenant.

title: Lord Gwyn's Firstborn
snippet:
Lord Gwyn's Firstborn -  Dark Souls - character - statues 
 statues : A statue of a mother holding a sword-wielding child, thought to represent the God of War, is located in front the Sunlight Altar bonfire. This statue also appears in several places, such as above the Firelink Altar and behind the coffin holding the Darkmoon Seance Ring. The sword the child is wielding shares a distinct resemblance to the Sunlight Straight Sword.

At the back of the room where Dragon Slayer Ornstein and Executioner Smough are fought, there are alcoves for three statues, with two of them depicting Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight and Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight, with the third one being empty. It is possible that this third alcove once held a statue depicting Gwyn's Firstborn, and was removed when he was expunged from the annals.

title: Ring of the Sun's Firstborn
snippet:
Ring of the Sun's Firstborn -  Dark Souls - ring - description 
 description : Lord Gwyn's firstborn, who inherited the sunlight, once wore this ancient ring. Boosts the strength of miracles.

Lord Gwyn's firstborn was a god of war, but his foolishness led to a loss of the annals, and rescinding of his deific status. Today, even his name is not known.

title: Archdragon Peak
snippet:
Archdragon Peak can be entered only after learning the Path of the Dragon gesture found upon a corpse of a Drakeblood Knight in the Consumed King's Garden; this faction of knights can be summoned in Archdragon Peak by the man serpents there. Drakeblood Knights worshiped the blood of dragons; and the red cloth decorating their armor is said to symbolize their yearning for blood.

In Archdragon Peak, the Calamity Ring is found, reportedly made from the orange eye of a calamitous dragon, the ring considered a symbol of dragon worship. This dragon was none other than Black Dragon Kalameet, said to be the last one of ancient dragons.

The Nameless King, known for once allying with ancient dragons, resides on Archdragon Peak. He is accompanied by a stormdrake, which he tamed and fought alongside him. Dragon Slayer Ornstein's weapon and armor can be found laying around the Nameless King's arena; he was said to have left his guard in Anor Londo cathedral to search for the Nameless King.

title: Archdragon Peak
snippet:
Archdragon Peak -  Dark Souls III - location - description 
 description : Archdragon Peak is an optional location that can be accessed by performing the "Path of the Dragon" gesture near the meditating dragon statue where the Dragon Torso Stone is found in the Irithyll Dungeon.

Archdragon Peak is populated by Man Serpents and Rock Lizards. It was seemingly built as a shrine to worship the Ancient Dragons by their descendants, the Man Serpents. Contrary to what its name implies, this area does not currently contain any true dragons, as those died long ago at the hands of the first Lords. The only dragons seemingly alive is the King of the Storm, the Nameless King's companion stormdrake mount, and the Ancient Wyverns. Archdragon Peak also overlooks on the body of an ancient dragon: the body can be seen clearly on the peak on the opposite side of the great bell.

The main boss of this area is The Nameless King.

title: Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight
snippet:
Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight -  Dark Souls III - character - trivia 
 trivia : "Gwynevere" is an English version of the French name "Guinevere", which is a version of the Welsh name "Gwenhwyfar" which translates from Welsh as "White Phantom".
According to the Arthurian Legend, Guinevere was the queen of Britain and was married to King Arthur. Her portrayal in literature has ranged from villainous and traitorous to a virtuous and noble woman.

title: The Nameless King
snippet:
The Nameless King -  Dark Souls III - boss - trivia 
 trivia : The soundtrack for the King of the Storm phase of the fight seems to borrow heavily from [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=grdraZc4wgI that of] the Ancient Dragon fight in *Dark Souls II*.

title: Great Lightning Spear (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Great Lightning Spear (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - spell - trivia 
 trivia : The "resplendent tale of father and son that while epic remains tragically untold" mentioned in the description is a reference to The Nameless King's losing his position as Gwyn's heir and his status as a God, thus making him unable to complete the story of the two generations of dragon-hunters.

title: Drangleic
snippet: From the day the king returned from his incursion into the land of the Giants, a dark shadow had gradually covered his expression, with even his vassals noticing a change in his character. The king of Drangleic became interested in the fate of other rulers of the past who might have found themselves in a situation similar to his and undertook expeditions on the ruins of the Brume Tower, Shulva and Frozen Eleum Loyce, but later decided to leave those lands cursed by several catastrophes, partially withdrawing his forces and sealing their access via magical altars.

title: Chancellor Wellager
snippet: However, the Giants would return with a vengance, and shortly after the king would vanish too. At some point after that, the chancellor would meet his end and linger on as a ghost, seemingly stuck in time and unable to move on, completely unaware of his current predicament.

title: Shira, Knight of Filianore
snippet: Shira would eventually have to quell a corruption that had been growing within the very city, caused by a mad king that had emerged among the other Pygmy Lords. When she tried to put him to rest, she realized that his body could not die, and he simply remained impaled to her cross spear, which began to be permeated with the king's dark power. As a result, Shira would bring her weapon to a darkroom, sealing the door shut and remaining by its side to ensure the king would remain put. Even in this prolonged captivity, the descendant of the Gods remained dignified, wearing her noble attire even though no one would see it.

title: The Old Chaos
snippet: The king made some attempts to combat the Chaos, and his knights delved valiantly into the depths to exterminate the terrible things that dwelled there, but not one of them returned. Eventually, the Ivory King sensed the degradation of his soul and left Eleum Loyce. He traveled deep into the Chaos with his knights until he was devoured by the flames.

title: Dragon
snippet:
The Nameless King is referenced to have sided with the Dragons and is speculated to be the first-born son of Gwyn, indicated by several descriptions on weapons and his boss soul. He is referenced as a dragon-slaying god of war who sacrificed everything to side with the Dragons, and Gwyn's first-born son is said to have been stripped of his stature as punishment for his foolishness and effectively removed from history as a result. When encountered, he is riding a Stormdrake, named King of the Storm.

Darkeater Midir is the only remaining dragon encountered in *Dark Souls III: The Ringed City.* Raised by the Gods of Lordran themselves to combat the growing Abyss, Midir's everlasting battle against the darkness has taken its toll on him, and he is slowly being consumed by the dark's influence. Fearing that the darkness within him may drive him mad, the Ashen One is tasked by Shira to put him down before he is lost to the Abyss.

title: Nameless Usurper

 lead : The **Nameless Usurper** is a Dark Spirit in *Dark Souls II*.

snippet:
Sunken King -  Dark Souls II - character - trivia 
 trivia : It's possible that Sinh consumed the Sunken King after it awoke, as his crown can only be retrieved once the dragon is felled, though it could just be a gameplay contrivance too.

title: Nameless Usurper
snippet:
Nameless Usurper -  Dark Souls II - enemy - description 
 description : The Nameless Usurper is a Dark Spirit that invades the player as they're traversing Drangleic Castle and later the Undead Crypt.
She dons the Saint's Set and fights with a Bandit's Knife.

title: Smelter Demon
snippet: The Smelter Demon found in the Iron Keep was responsible for the death of the Old Iron King, and by extension the full fall of his kingdom. Although his existence as the man he was before ended, the King became a golem-like being himself, possessed by an incredibly powerful soul that lurked below the magma.

title: Crown of the Sunken King (helm)
snippet:
Crown of the Sunken King (helm) -  Dark Souls II - armor - description 
 description : Crown of the Sunken King who once ruled this land.

The King erected the Eternal Sanctum below the earth to worship the great dragon, but the towering bulwark crumbled with the city shortly after the dragon's awakening.

But these were events of long ago, and today, no one even remembers the King's name.

title: King's Crown
snippet:
King's Crown -  Dark Souls II - armor - description 
 description : Crown of Vendrick, King of Drangleic.

What makes a king? Some say that it is birthright, while others call it destiny.

Perhaps it is not important, as long as the king's name serves to unite his people.

title: Four Kings
snippet:
Four Kings -  Dark Souls - boss - trivia 
 trivia : The Four Kings' title uses the kanji "公王", a term that was used to define a nobleman that married a daughter of the King.
The sword used by the Four Kings was intended to be in the game, however, it was removed from the final version of the game.
The Four Kings are the only holders of a Lord Soul or Bequeathed Lord Soul Shard that are not shown in the opening cinematic.
The name of the boss may reference a group of 1980s boxing legends also known as the Four Kings. One of them, Sugar Ray Leonard, is referenced in the Rayleonard Corporation of *Armored Core 4* and *For Answer*. Ironically, however, the Four Kings are weaker when at close range.

title: Drangleic
snippet: Vendrick fled the Castle through the King's Passage never to return, fearing Nashandra's wickedness. He left the Looking Glass Knight behind him, ready to expunge those who would challenge him, forever true to his original command, as the first line of defense against those who would attempt to pursue the runaway king into the Undead Crypt. The king took with him only a handful of Royal Soldiers and the faithful Sir Velstadt, and found refuge in the Shrine of Amana. Vendrick was initially intent on reaching the Throne of Want and link the First Flame but in the end the king understood that if he did so, Nashandra would have gained an easy access to the throne connected to the Flame. Vendrick thus decided to free himself from his soul, abandoning it among the ruins, to descend even deeper into the Undead Crypt. Here, left alone, he isolated himself in a secluded room wearing only his robes, crown, sword and his ring. Overcome by nihilism, Vendrick was consumed by the curse and soon

title: Ancient Dragon
snippet: Rumors abound in Drangleic about the king's brother, Lord Aldia, who tried to create a dragon. Perhaps the existence of the Ancient Dragon, and its dubious origins, are testament to his success.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
The Bearer of the Curse will journey through the Black Gulch to find the fallen kingdom of Shulva, Sanctum City, once ruled by the Sunken King. The king ruled the city, centred around the worship of a slumbering dragon known as Sinh, until his kingdom was invaded by the Drakeblood Knights lead by Sir Yorgh, who sought to claim the dragon's blood. Sir Yorgh slew the king, and awoke the dragon, which proceeded to kill him and lay waste to the city with its poison. The Bearer of the Curse slays Elana, the Squalid Queen, a child of the Abyss, and the dragon Sinh to claim the Sunken King's crown.

Next, the Bearer of the Curse returns to the Old Iron Kingdom, to seek the Old Iron King's crown. Finding the kingdom under the sway of another child of the Abyss, Nadalia, Bride of Ash, the Bearer braves their way through the ruined towers to find the Fume Knight, who guards the crown of the Old Iron King.

title: Crown of the Ivory King (helm)
snippet:
Crown of the Ivory King (helm) -  Dark Souls II - armor - description 
 description : Crown of the Ivory King who once ruled this land.

Far to the north, a King built a great cathedral to appease the raging flame. But when he sensed the degradation of his soul, he left without a word, leaving everything to Alsanna, who had, unbeknownst, found a place at his side.

But these were events of long ago, and today, no one even remembers the King's name.

title: Lothric
snippet: the state of his kingdom to protect the "child of dragons", the culmination of his desires and the only thing left in his life. Despite his efforts, the king was not even able to see Ocelotte, merely holding him tightly in his palm. Moreover, the secrets of the moonlight, central to his frenzied search, eluded him in the end.

title: Burnt Ivory King
snippet:
At an unknown point, an ancient Chaos was discovered deep below the land. Legend holds that the Ivory King used his magnificent soul to build Eleum Loyce and contain the spread of Chaos. A grand cathedral was built in an attempt to appease the raging flame, but the Chaos would not be sated. As a precaution, various knights and golems were posted throughout the Garrison Ward to lead the advance on the swollen flame on his orders. Other knights were ordered to delve into the depths of Chaos to exterminate the terrible things that dwelt there, but not one of the knights returned.

Eventually, the Ivory King sensed the degradation of his soul and left Eleum Loyce without a word, leaving everything to Alsanna. He traveled deep into the Chaos until he and his knights were corrupted by the flames. At some point after the King's departure, the ivory gates of the city were flung open, and the land grew cold and lifeless.

title: Drangleic
snippet: Centuries after the end of Vendrick's reign, Drangleic would be known in Lothric as "Drang", the land of the legend of the Linking of the Fire. Vendrick's name has been lost to history, who is remembered only as the "Old King of Want", an ancient ruler that was cursed by an all-consuming thirst, making him no king at all in the end. The Dragonriders of his royal guard and their immense strength are also properly remembered. A group of soldiers, who proclaimed themselves descendants of Drangleic and wore the geisteel armor made by the blacksmith of Vendrick's Castle, abandoned the region and became sellswords. Known as Drang Knights, they scattered across the lands and quickly became known for shieldless, aggressive fighting tactics that utilized twinspears and hammers, striking fear into the hearts of their enemies.

title: Frozen Eleum Loyce
snippet:
In addition the Ivory King was served by seven beasts infused with wondrous souls and each of them were conferred a specific duty. Aava became the guardian of Alsanna as the King's beloved child while Lud and Zallen were tasked with the mercy killing of exiles

However the flames of Chaos would not be sated and the Ivory King was forced to use the power of his own soul to keep it at bay. Over time he was drained of his vigour and when he sensed the degradation of his power he decided to plunge into Chaos' heart in an attempt to reduce its flames alone. He decided to leave without a word to his subjects and left everything to Alsanna who had now found her place at his side, conferring a sword inscribed with the name of the land to her. In the end, despite the remnants of his strong soul, even the Ivory King lost the battle against Chaos and was devoured by its flames, becoming an empty husk controlled by them.

title: Nashandra
snippet: When Drangleic was ravaged by the second war with the giants and the spread of the Undead Curse, Vendrick came to realize the true nature and identity of Nashandra, and what she had coveted all along. Knowing that his time was short and that his queen had to be stopped, Vendrick created several impasses that would prevent Nashandra from seizing the throne, and sealed himself away in the Undead Crypt. This left Nashandra the sole ruler of Drangleic, albeit without much left to rule at all, as the kingdom had been all but destroyed.

title: Gods
snippet:
McLoyf, God of Medicine and Alcoholic Drinks. He is nicknamed 'Old Man' McLloyf, although it is not his official title.
Fina, a Goddess who possesses fateful beauty but whose embracing love is as fickle as the weather..
The Nameless Blacksmith Deity, who forged the weapons of the Old Gods and died before the events of *Dark Souls*; the Titanite Demons (whom, in spite of their name, are not actual demons) were born from his death. It is unclear if he ever had a name, and although he is called a god in item descriptions, it is unclear if he was worshipped or part of the Way of White.
By the events of *Dark Souls*, a God was banished for being "incorrigibly covetous" and cursed into becoming the first Mimic.

title: Knight King Rendal
snippet:
Knight King Rendal -  Dark Souls III - character - trivia 
 trivia : In *Demon's Souls*, [https://demonssouls.fandom.com/wiki/Old_King_Allant Old King Allant's] model is internally labeled "**レンドル王**" which translates to "*King Rendal*", the same name of the legendary Knight King of *Dark Souls*. Whether this was done intentionally by the developers or not remains a mystery.
**With the japanese script itself using internal names sporadically, Ostrava refers to his father Allant as "King Rendal" in his final dialogue.

title: Oceiros, the Consumed King
snippet: In his later years, frustrated by continuous failures to find a worthy Champion, Oceiros was driven to insanity by his work with Lothric's blood and became fascinated with dragons and sought other means of achieving his goal. Eventually, Oceiros turned to the cursed knowledge of the Grand Archives, where he found the twisted worship of Seath, developing a fascination for the Pale Dragon, his mad research and the secrets of his moonlight. His newfound devotion was testified by his dragonscale ring, which he claimed protected him from his enemies, and his army's usage of shields decorated with a white dragon. His fascination soon became obsession, which progressed to insanity. The loss of his sanity in the pursuit of the ways of the White Dragon would earn him the name "Consumed King" and many assassins were sent to remove the king from power, none of whom succeeded, owing according to Oceiros to the divine protection of his dragonscale ring.

title: Furtive Pygmy
snippet: With this clever move Gwyn ensured the subjugation of the Pygmy Lords, their Dark Soul trapped inside the Ringed City and expunged from the annals. Even the contributions of the Ringed Knights during the war against the dragons were erased from history, as well as the very existence of the Pygmy.

title: Sunlight Medal
snippet:
Sunlight Medal -  Dark Souls - item - description 
 description : This faintly warm medal, engraved with the symbol of the Sun, is the ultimate honor, awarded to those who summon the Warrior of Sunlight and complete a goal.

The symbol represents Lord Gwyn's firstborn, who lost his deity status and was expunged from the annals. But the old God of War still watches closely over his warriors.

title: Nameless Blacksmith Deity
snippet:
Nameless Blacksmith Deity -  Dark Souls - character - dark_souls_ii 
 dark_souls_ii : As their name had already disappeared from the annals of history in the era of Lordran, their existence is completely obscured in Drangleic. Despite this, Titanite was seen as a divine gift in all its forms, and it was believed that Titanite Slabs were what provided the world with it originally. Legends also still speak of them being used to forge the gods' arsenal.

title: Ring of the Sun's First Born
snippet:
Ring of the Sun's First Born -  Dark Souls III - ring - description 
 description : Ring of the Sun's first born, who inherited the light of Gwyn, the first lord.

Greatly boosts miracles.

The Sun's first born was once a god of war, until he was stripped of his stature as punishment for his foolishness. No wonder his very name has slipped from the annals of history.

title: Lords
snippet:
Lords -  Dark Souls II - character - aftermath 
 aftermath : Seath was driven to madness as a result of his experiments and accrued knowledge. His attendants would kidnap humans from across the land to be experimented on and even the maidens of Gwynevere. Eventually he discovered a kind of immortality, being invincible so long as the crystal remained. Through the knowledge accumulated by Seath, the human sorcerer Logan would be able to craft new spells and further augment his own spells, though he too would be driven mad much like Seath was.

At some point the Gwyn's firstborn betrayed the gods and allied with the descendants of the dragons, and his name was stripped from him, being removed from all recorded history such as annals and statues.

title: Sir Alonne
snippet:
Sir Alonne -  Dark Souls II - boss - lore 
 lore : Sir Alonne is a wandering swordsman and formerly the Iron King's right-hand man. Alonne came from the east and chose to serve the Iron King and help establish his own kingdom. When the Iron King was at the peak of his rule, Sir Alonne left him to travel the lands for an unknown reason. For his service the Iron King bestowed Alonne's name to his knights.

title: Milfanito
snippet:
==Trivia==
As with Gravelord Nito, their implied creator, the Milfanito's name could be a play on the Italian word finito, meaning "ended."
The Milfanito located before the Demon of Song's fog gate appears weak and will not converse with the player. This is likely related to the Demon itself, in which she may have narrowly escaped death from the creature.
The song the Milfanito sing is a rendition of the Nameless Song, which was the end-credits theme in the original *Dark Souls''.

title: Dragonslayer Swordspear
snippet:
Dragonslayer Swordspear -  Dark Souls III - weapon - description 
 description : A dragon hunting weapon from the age of the gods. The earliest form of the cross spear, serving as both sword and spear.

Its owner was the Nameless King and deific hunter of dragons. The swordspear is imbued with lightning, of which he was the heir.

Skill: Falling Bolt
Hold swordspear high in the air to summon fierce lightning that descends upon distant foes.

title: Crossbreed Priscilla
snippet:
**Gwyndolin's final thoughts of a "white girl", as he was devoured by Aldrich, allow the creation of a miracle that replicates the Lifehunt Scythe of Priscilla; as miracles are tales of the gods, it would mean that Gwyndolin had a special relationship with Priscilla and remembered her before his demise.
**Gwyndolin's legitimacy as a deity came only from the fact that he was the son of King Gwyn, implying that his matrilineage alone would not have had him considered among the deities, as she was not one.
**Gwyndolin being Priscilla's son, as she was hated and feared by the gods, would explain why Gwyn would dress, educate and raise him to be a female, as the king of the gods would not have wanted him to be able to ascend the throne with his dangerous lineage.

title: Dragonscale Set
snippet:
Dragonscale Set -  Dark Souls III - armor - description 
 description : Armor of a nameless king who was ally to the ancient dragons.

The golden crown, buried amidst long strands of bristling ash, is said to closely resemble that of the First Lord.

title: Golden Bracelets
snippet:
Golden Bracelets -  Dark Souls III - armor - description 
 description : Bracelets of a nameless king who was ally to the ancient dragons.

These golden bracelets, together with the golden breastplate and crown, are said to closely resemble those of the First Lord.

title: Lords
snippet:
In his fear of the Age of Dark, he sacrificed himself to the First Flame, prolonging the Age of Fire and becoming Lord of Cinder. This act rendered Gwyn Hollow.

At some point, his firstborn son tamed a stormdrake, and allied with the dragon descendants. For this treachery, he was stripped of his godhood and banished (albeit, not by Gwyn), expunged from all records of history.

title: Eleum Loyce
snippet:
Eleum Loyce -  Dark Souls II - weapon - description 
 description : Curved sword forged from the soul of Alsanna.
Formed by two curious blades,
this sword can restore an ally's HP
with a hit from its strong attack.

The enigmatic Alsanna quietly found a place
at the Ivory King's side, and when his strength
was fully drained, he conferred this sword,
inscribed with the name of the land, to her.

title: Eygil
snippet: If this were true, then the sins that the Lost Sinner constantly punishes herself for could include the aforemantiond creation of the Smelter Demon, mirroring the Witch of Izalith's own conceit leading to the creation of the demon race. Why Eygil would be imprisoned in the Lost Bastille, a place belonging to the rival kingdom of Venn, is unclear, though the Old Iron King may have conquered it just as he conquered the land where Brume Tower was erected. Alternatively, they may have just captured and imprisoned the magus when the king perished and his kingdom fell.

title: Bewitched Alonne Sword
snippet:
Bewitched Alonne Sword -  Dark Souls II - weapon - description 
 description : Katana forged from the soul of Sir Alonne. The captivating, undulating design serves to enhance this weapon's mystical allure.

Alonne came from the east, and soon became the Iron King's most trusted knight. When he departed, the Old Iron King bequeathed Sir Alonne's name to his iron warriors.

title: Dragonslayer Spear (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Dragonslayer Spear (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - availability 
 availability : Found in Archdragon Peak. From the Dragon-Kin Mausoleum bonfire, proceed up the nearby stairs and the spear can be obtained by interacting with the metal gate that leads to the courtyard below the Nameless King's arena.

title: Eygil
snippet:
Eygil -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - trivia 
 trivia : Eygil's name may be a reference to the Arabic word "عجل" (pronounced "ijl"), which means calf, the offspring of a bull. It is potentially relevant due to the sheer quantity of bull imagery featured in the Old Iron King's domain, and the magus' connection to the symbol through the idol in the Iron Keep.
The Primal Bonfire found after defeating the Old Iron King is internally named "Eygil's Altar".
Before the *Crown of the Old Iron King DLC* formally introduced the magus as a character, some people believed Eygil to be the Old Iron King's real name.

title: Havel's Armor (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Havel's Armor (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - armor - description 
 description : Armor as if hewn from a giant boulder.
Offers stupendous defense, but weighs a ton.

The origin of the name Havel is not clear.
Some say it was the warrior who wore the armor,
but others say that it was the name of a great
kingdom ruined in a barbaric war.
